title: Why I stopped touching the code
author: whyNamesTurkiye
selftext:
I used to make small code changes myself because it seemed more economical. Lately, though, every manual edit feels like interference. The AI doesn't always understand my style or intent, so my changes can break its workflow. I've found it's better not to touch the code myself anymore. What do you think?

My last game with code I wrote myself: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/4277100/Batelus/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4277100/Batelus/)

comments.author: Am_Biyori
comments.body: It troubles me that you're afraid to go against the AIs choices when they go against what you want because you think it will break its work flow. Making the changes you want it to make should always be part of its workflow.

replies.author: whyNamesTurkiye
replies.body: It is clearly not what I am talking about, If something is not in a way I want I would tell him. I am talking about manually changing the code

replies.author: weeknie
replies.body:
And you manually changing the code is exactly what the commenter meant by "going against the AIs choices", since the AI made a choice to write the code that way.

I definitely agree with the comment, you being afraid to make changes in your code is a red flag to me. Also, I don't really see why the AI would have an issue with you making changes anyway

replies.author: Am_Biyori
replies.body: Ok. I get what you're saying. I do have trouble looking at it as a 'him'. 'It' is a computer program that will make due with whatever you give it, either by prompt or by giving it you own editions to the code. All I'm saying is not to worry about interfering with it because your job is to interfere with it if you're not happy with the script.

comments.author: neon_joyful_horizon
comments.body: your instinct is right. Letting the AI handle execution and saving yourself for architecture decisions prevents context rot. Treat the code as a disposable draft rather than a sacred text you need to polish by hand.

comments.author: Navadvisor
comments.body: There's just little point in looking at the code anymore, it's an irrelevant implementation detail. The AI is 100 times faster and much more accurate. You need to hold it's feet to the fire on the quality of the product it's making but looking at the code you can't build the context up in any reasonable time.

replies.author: Infamous-Bed-7535
replies.body:
100x faster in generating, but it is not 100x faster to get the code be generated the way you want.

Accuracy, not bad, but definitely not much more accurate, easily can introduce akward errors.
The major problem is code quality, especially if you give it lot of freedom.

I use ai, but the direction that is full agentic, code is not meant to be read by humans is absurd.
Giving up on these will have its price especially on tech debt, including cognitive one.

replies.author: Navadvisor
replies.body: The AIs cognition is cheaper and faster than yours, and it's just getting better and better. Like 6 months ago I'd be with you but it's so over for this perspective with astra, Fable, sol 6.1 and opus 5.5. if there's something in the code causing a problem have the AI investigate and refactor it if it needs it. It feels like arrogance or ignorance to me to be able to believe there will still be a place for humans to read code anywhere in the near future. I still think there is a place for a technologically minded person who understands the business, the domain, side of things, at least for now. I don't know what that's going to look like in 3 years because to digest the revolution we've already had would take years but it's just going to keep coming.

replies.author: Infamous-Bed-7535
replies.body:
Cheaper.. yeah check the balance sheets of these companies :)

We are the lock in phase.
I can imagine that models will stop working on sources that were generated by rival models and Trump figures out that any commit having 'contributed by xy' is rightful to be accessed by the AI companies, etc..

Companies are mindlessly outsourcing their know how and the solutions that gives them the edge on the market and share with non trustworthy companies.

It is not that straightforward.

replies.author: Navadvisor
replies.body: Hiring software engineers is pretty expensive too, a lot more expensive.

replies.author: Infamous-Bed-7535
replies.body:
I will keep working in mixed setup, about to do some experiments with fully agentic setup as I have a pretty good workflow in my head.
BUT I will still working normally. I like to understand and create new things, enjoy learning and do not want to burn out.

We will need capable humans in the loop. Probably much less than now, but knowledge and experience gives an edge even in the usage of the Ai.

So would be a huge mistake IMO to give up practicing your brain and skills.

replies.author: Infamous-Bed-7535
replies.body:
I would also argue that code quality does not matter anymore.
It is easier and CHEAPER for any Ai to work a much smaller codebase, where touching a single part won't break 5 logically independent modules.
Yeah ai can work it out, but there will be significant amount of difference in token efficiency.

replies.author: siberianmi
replies.body:
So set the quality bars you want and tell it to meet them.

Force it to benchmark its code, write tests, eliminate all lint warnings, etc etc.

AI will relentlessly pursue whatever quality bars you see and provide it a way to measure.

replies.author: Economy_Bedroom3902
replies.body:
You can ask the AI to assist with explaining the context.

I personally find you do still need to look at the code to ensure your automated quality validator gates are configured correctly, so the AI catches problems earlier.

comments.author: BangEnergyFTW
comments.body: We don't look at code anymore. We just burn electricity until it works.

comments.author: ZymzAlchemy
comments.body:
I guardrail my agent so it's only allowed to code in my style, then I always verify and correct the phases once they are complete. I never let the agent make their own decisions. It always ends up bad when the scope grows. YMMV. 

Be well, keep creating.
